He played [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]]. Anderson was selected with the 21st overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[New Jersey Nets]], who traded him to the [[Orlando Magic]] in June 2009. With the Magic, he received the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] in 2012. In July 2012, Anderson was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]], who changed their name to the Pelicans in April 2013. In July 2016, he signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] as a free agent and was dealt to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in August 2018. Anderson was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in February 2019 and returned to the Rockets in September of the same year before being waived two months later. == Early life == Anderson was born in [[Sacramento, California]] and attended [[Oak Ridge High School (El Dorado Hills, California)|Oak Ridge High School]] in nearby [[El Dorado Hills, California|El Dorado Hills]].{{cite web | url = http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/ryan-anderson/gNlyDfTlEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm | title = Ryan Anderson | work = MaxPreps.com | access-date = January 8, 2016}} His parents are Jack Anderson and Sue Anderson and he is very close to his grandparents. == High school career == In 2005, Anderson helped lead the Oak Ridge Trojans to the Division II California State Championship. The game was held at [[ARCO Arena]] in Sacramento. In the opening round of that playoff series, Anderson's No. 1 ranked team narrowly averted an upset against a [[John H. Pitman High School]] team led by [[Colin Kaepernick]], who would later go on to become an NFL quarterback for the [[San Francisco 49ers]].[http://www.maxpreps.com/games/basketball-winter-05-06/oak-ridge-vs-pitman/2-22-2006-1AjTQLbnRkOEOgncM4BXrA.htm Game Details: Pitman @ Oak Ridge Basketball 2/22/06] In that game, Kaepernick scored 34 points while Anderson scored 50.[http://www.calbears.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30100&ATCLID=208187432 Ryan Anderson Bio] Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Anderson was listed as the No. 22 power forward and the No. 98 player in the nation in 2006.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Ryan-Anderson-41547 Ryan Anderson – Yahoo! Sports] == College career == Anderson played two seasons for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] at [[UC Berkeley]], averaging 18.7 points and 9.0 rebounds in 33.0 minutes per game in 66 career games.{{cite web |title=Breaking down Cal alumni in the NBA: Jaylen Brown, Ryan Anderson and Allen Crabbe {{!}} The Daily Californian |url=http://www.dailycal.org/2017/06/14/breaking-cal-alumni-nba-jaylen-brown-ryan-anderson-allen-crabbe/ |website=The Daily Californian |date=June 14, 2017}}{{cite web |title=CalBears.com {{!}} University of California Official Athletic Site |url=https://calbears.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5270 |website=calbears.com}} As a freshman in 2006–07, he led the Bears in scoring and rebounding, averaging 16.3 points and 8.2 rebounds, and earned Honorable Mention All-Pac-10 honors. He went on to be named Second Team All-America by The Sporting News and earned First Team All-Pac-10 honors as a sophomore in 2007–08. He led the Pac-10 in scoring, averaging 21.1 points (ranked 18th in nation) and ranked third in rebounding, pulling down 9.9 rebounds per game. On April 3, 2008, Anderson declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3328301 Cal sophomore Anderson will try NBA draft] == Professional career == === New Jersey Nets (2008–2009) === [[File:Ryan Anderson cropped.jpg|thumb|Anderson with the Nets in 2009]] On June 26, 2008, Anderson was selected with the 21st overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[New Jersey Nets]]. He made his NBA debut on October 29, 2008, against the [[Washington Wizards]]. He played in 66 games during his rookie campaign with New Jersey, averaging 7.4 points and 4.7 rebounds in 19.9 minutes per game, as he ranked 10th among all NBA rookies in three-point field-goal percentage (.365 – 69-of-189). === Orlando Magic (2009–2012) === [[File:RyanAndersonMagic.jpg|thumb|Anderson with the Magic in 2010]] On June 25, 2009, Anderson was traded, along with [[Vince Carter]], to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Rafer Alston]], [[Tony Battie]] and [[Courtney Lee]].{{cite web | title = Orlando Acquires Vince Carter and Ryan Anderson From New Jersey | url = http://www.nba.com/magic/news/blockbustertrade_carter_062509.html | work = NBA.com | date = June 25, 2009 | access-date = June 27, 2009}} In 2009–10, he appeared in 63 games with Orlando, averaging 7.7 points and 3.2 rebounds in 14.5 minutes per game. He started in six games during the regular season, and played in a further nine playoff games. In 2010–11, Anderson played in 64 games (14 starts) with Orlando, averaging 10.6 points and 5.5 rebounds in 22.3 minutes per game. During December 2010, he missed nine games due to a sprained right foot.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderry01/gamelog/2011/ Ryan Anderson 2010-11 Game Log] In the lockout-shortened 2011–12 season, Anderson won the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] after averaging 16.1 points and 7.7 rebounds in 61 games.[http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/04/most-improved-player/ Magic's Ryan Anderson wins Kia Most Improved Player Award] He led the NBA in both three-point field goals made and attempted, while ranking seventh in free throw percentage, tied for 27th in three-point field goal percentage, ranking 29th in rebounding and 33rd in scoring. === New Orleans Hornets / Pelicans (2012–2016) === [[File:Ryan Anderson Hornets.jpg|thumb|Anderson with the Hornets in 2013]] On July 11, 2012, Anderson was acquired by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in a sign-and-trade deal that sent [[Gustavo Ayón]] to the Magic.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_acquire_ryan_anderson_2012_07_10.html|title=HORNETS ACQUIRE RYAN ANDERSON|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012}} During his first season for the Hornets in 2012–13, he appeared in 81 games (22 starts) and averaged 16.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game. He finished second in the NBA with a career-high 213 three-point field goals made in 557 attempts (38.2%).{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderry01/gamelog/2013/|title=Ryan Anderson 2012–13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 11, 2014}} In April 2013, the Hornets changed their name to the Pelicans.[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-officially-adopt-new-namesake NEW ORLEANS PELICANS OFFICIALLY ADOPT NEW NAMESAKE] On December 2, 2013, Anderson scored a career-high 36 points in a 131–128 triple overtime win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20131202/NOPCHI/gameinfo.html Notebook: Pelicans 131, Bulls 128 (3OT)] On January 3, 2014, Anderson suffered a neck injury colliding with [[Gerald Wallace]] in the Pelicans' 95–92 win over the [[Boston Celtics]]. Anderson, who had to be removed from the court on a stretcher, required neck surgery and was ruled out for the rest of the season in late March.{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2014/03/25/ryan-anderson-neck-surgery-injury-update-new-orleans-pelicans|title=Pelicans' Ryan Anderson to undergo season-ending neck surgery|work=SI.com|last=Golliver|first=Ben|date=March 25, 2014|access-date=April 11, 2014}} He managed just 22 games in 2013–14, averaging 19.8 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. On October 28, 2014, Anderson made his return for the Pelicans in their season-opening game against the Orlando Magic. In 22 minutes of action, he recorded 22 points and 9 rebounds off the bench in a 101–84 win.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141028/ORLNOP/gameinfo.html |title=Davis power Pelicans past Magic, 101-84 | work=NBA.com | date=October 28, 2014 | access-date=October 28, 2014}} On February 22, 2015, he was ruled out for two to four weeks after being diagnosed with an MCL sprain in his right knee.[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-injury-update Pelicans Injury Update] He returned to action on April 1 and played out the regular season, and appeared in the team's four playoff games. Anderson continued to be an effective role player off the bench for the Pelicans in 2015–16. On January 15, 2016, he scored a then season-high 32 points and hit six three-pointers in a 109–107 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20160115/CHANOP/gameinfo.html Anderson, Davis, lead Pelicans past Hornets, 109-107] On January 23, he scored 23 points and tied a season high with six three-pointers in a 116–99 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. In that game, the Pelicans hit a franchise-best 17 three-pointers.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160123/MILNOP/gameinfo.html Anderson shoots way to 23 points, Pelicans beat Bucks 116-99] On January 28, he scored 30 of his career high-tying 36 points in the first half of the Pelicans' 114–105 win over the Sacramento Kings. Starting in just his seventh game of the season, at power forward in place of the injured [[Anthony Davis]], Anderson's 30 first half points set a franchise record.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160128/SACNOP/gameinfo.html Anderson scores 36, leads Pelicans past Kings, 114-105] After being diagnosed with a sports hernia in late March, Anderson missed the team's final 14 games of the season.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderry01/gamelog/2016/ Ryan Anderson 2015–16 Game Log] === Houston Rockets (2016–2018) === On July 9, 2016, Anderson signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agents-ryan-anderson-and-eric-gordon|title=Rockets Sign Free Agents Ryan Anderson and Eric Gordon|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2016}} He made his debut for the Rockets in their season opener on October 26, recording 14 points and six rebounds in a 120–114 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderry01/gamelog/2017/|title=Ryan Anderson 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 18, 2016}} On December 1, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 132–127 double overtime win over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On December 23, he set a new season high with 31 points in a 115–109 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899890|title=Conley scores 24 points, Grizzlies beat Rockets 115-109|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2016|access-date=December 23, 2016}} During the [[2017 NBA playoffs]], Anderson scored 19 points during a 110–107 overtime WCSF Game Five loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].[https://www.yahoo.com/news/ginobili-soars-deny-harden-rockets-spurs-thriller-032948533--nba.html Ginobili thwarts Rockets in NBA playoffs with stunning block] Houston eventually lost the series in six games.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/HOU/2017.html 2016-17 Houston Rockets Roster and Stats] During the 2017 offseason, the Rockets began working to move Anderson's large contract. To clear the way for a trade out of Houston during the 2018 offseason, Anderson agreed to reduce the guarantee on his $21 million salary in 2019–20 to $15.6 million.{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=August 31, 2018 |title=Rockets trade Ryan Anderson, De'Anthony Melton to Suns, sources say web |title=Suns Acquire Ryan Anderson and De'Anthony Melton from Houston |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-acquire-ryan-anderson-and-deanthony-melton-houston |website=NBA.com
